All 10 backend pytest cases passed. Frontend flows verified end-to-end including delete confirm dialog & row removal.

ui_bugs.issue: Stale-closure bug in form state: `const set = (k) => (e) => setForm({ ...form, [k]: e.target.value })` reads `form` from closure at render time. When multiple fields are populated quickly (fast typing / autofill / browser password managers), later field's onChange spreads a stale `form` and can overwrite earlier field values (e.g. name got blanked when subsequent fields were typed). Reproduced in Playwright with page.fill on 5 fields in rapid succession — the `name` field ended up empty. Recommended fix: use functional setState — `setForm(f => ({ ...f, [k]: e.target.value }))`.

action_items: Fix PublicDemo.jsx stale-closure in set() — replace with functional setState (setForm(f => ({...f, [k]: e.target.value}))) to prevent field values being clobbered when users type/paste quickly across fields.

rca of the issue: PublicDemo.jsx bug RCA: `set = (k) => (e) => setForm({ ...form, [k]: e.target.value })` — `form` is captured in the closure at each render. Between rapid keystrokes on different fields, if React hasn't yet committed the previous state update, the new onChange handler still spreads the stale `form`, overwriting previously typed values. Repro: use Playwright page.fill on all 5 inputs back-to-back — `name` ends up empty. Mitigation: functional setState (`setForm(f => ({...f, [k]: e.target.value}))`).
